intro: The analysis below summarizes the reported experiences of candidates who took the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 6 October 2026. Shift 1 and Shift 2 have partial data, while Shift 3 has not yet been conducted and its analysis will be added after the shift. Figures such as good‑attempt percentages are unofficial and may vary between sources. The SSC normalises scores across shifts to ensure comparability.

shifts.summary: Reports gave mixed views on overall difficulty, describing it as moderate or easy to moderate, and estimated good attempts between 78 and 82‑94. Reasoning was called easy or moderate, with many questions repeated from previous years; GA was seen as easy to moderate, focusing on static GK, current affairs and history. Quant was rated easy to moderate, with geometry, mensuration, trigonometry and algebra featured; English was rated moderate to difficult, with editorial‑based reading comprehension, vocabulary and idioms. Candidates said the section timer caused time management problems, especially in maths, and some reported mouse or click issues.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Very easy, mostly repeated from previous year papers

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Advanced maths heavy (10-12 questions), lengthy and calculative, time management issue due to section timer

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: No Cloze Test, passage lengthy and editorial based, vocab moderate

observations: Section timer caused time management problems, especially in Maths.
Mouse/click issues: double click required, lag causing repeated clicks, auto‑next after a few seconds.
Paper was based on previous year questions.
Some felt cutoff may go low due to timer issues.
disagreements: Overall difficulty: reports differ (Moderate vs Easy to Moderate).
Overall good attempts: reports differ (82‑94 vs 78).
Reasoning difficulty: reports differ (Easy vs Moderate).
GA difficulty: reports differ (Easy to Moderate vs Easy).

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty reported for the 6 October 2026 exam in Shift 1?
faqs.a: Candidates described the difficulty of Shift 1 as ranging from moderate to easy to moderate. The reports indicated mixed views, with some sections perceived as easier than others.

faqs.q: How did candidates rate the difficulty of Shift 2 on 6 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 2 was reported as easy overall, and each of the four sections – reasoning, general ability, quantitative, and English – was also described as easy.

faqs.q: When will the analysis for Shift 3 of the 6 October 2026 exam be available?
faqs.a: Shift 3 has not yet been held. Its analysis will be added after the shift is conducted.

faqs.q: Are the good‑attempt percentages for the 6 October 2026 exam reliable?
faqs.a: The good‑attempt percentages are unofficial and differ between sources. They should be taken as approximate indicators rather than exact figures.

faqs.q: How does the SSC handle score comparison across different shifts for the 6 October 2026 exam?
faqs.a: The SSC normalises scores across shifts, which allows candidates' results to be compared fairly regardless of the shift they attended.
